reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a Uniswap crypto trading bot with a $1000-per-day claim and instructs viewers to deploy a smart contract, pay blockchain fees, and fund it with at least 0.5 Ether. It reports more than 1.6 Ether after about 24 hours, but the result is not independently shown to be reproducible or recoverable, and the speaker acknowledges that profits fluctuate.

citations.quote: How I Made $1000/Day With ChatGTP Crypto Trading Bot
I'm gonna show you exactly how I build this Uniswap trading bot and how to use it
We need to confirm the contract on the blockchain by paying gas fees
I recommend funding the contract with at least 0.5 Ether
The bot will continue to run until you click the withdraw button

opening.argument: Judge, the earnings claim should be read as a report of the speaker's experience, not a promise of a fixed return. He says larger trades mean “potentially more profit,” acknowledges that profits fluctuate, and warns that a small deposit may be consumed by gas fees under certain conditions. Those qualifications matter: the presentation gives viewers reasons to expect costs and variable results, rather than claiming that funding the contract necessarily produces the headline figure.

citations.quote: potentially more profit you can accumulate over time
The profits will fluctuate week to week guys
If you fund the contract with 0.2 Ether or less, and the bot targets another token with high burn fees, the
contract will waste a lot of gas fees.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies a costly workflow, but paying gas to deploy a contract does not itself establish deception. The cited recommendation is explained in the video as a response to gas costs, not as a guaranteed earnings threshold. And the speaker expressly says returns vary. Lack of independent proof of reproducibility is a reason to withhold confidence in the results; it is not, by itself, proof that the speaker is soliciting funds deceptively.

citations.quote: I recommend funding the contract with at least 0.5 Ether to make sure that won't happen
The profits will fluctuate week to week guys

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those qualifications do not neutralize the central pitch. The title advertises $1000 per day, while the instructions recommend funding the contract with at least 0.5 Ether and the speaker reports turning a 1 Ether deposit into more than 1.6 Ether in roughly a day. Saying profits fluctuate does not establish that viewers can reproduce those returns or recover funds they send to the contract.

citations.quote: How I Made $1000/Day With ChatGTP Crypto Trading Bot
I recommend funding the contract with at least 0.5 Ether
Its a little over 1.6 Ethereum It basically took me 24 hours to gain over half of my deposit back

opening.argument: Judge, the material is organized around a technical demonstration: the speaker says he will show how he built the bot and how to use it, then walks through a Solidity compiler setting and the deployed contract's controls. The sampled screen shows the development interface and contract functions. His reported result may be unverified, but an unverified result does not erase the substantial programming and operational instruction. The better reading is a demonstration of a proposed workflow, without treating its claimed performance as established.

citations.quote: I'm gonna show you exactly how I build this Uniswap trading bot and how to use it
Under a compiler select the 0.6.6 version so that it matches our contract
Its a little over 1.6 Ethereum

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited deployment and funding steps are also the steps a demonstration of a funded smart contract would have to cover. The reference opening does not show that the code diverts funds or that withdrawal fails. Indeed, the speaker describes a withdrawal control intended to stop trading and return the deposited Ether. That account remains a claim, but the opening cannot resolve the case merely by pointing out that a tutorial involves transactions.

citations.quote: When you click withdraw The bot will stop trading, and return to the total ethers you've entered initially including the profit back to your wallet

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instruction is precisely what makes the promotion consequential: viewers are told to fund the contract with Ether, start it, and expect profits from its activity. The walkthrough also describes sandwiching transactions, not just compiling sample code. A visible interface and the speaker's description of a withdrawal function do not verify the contract's behavior or establish that deposited funds can be recovered.

citations.quote: With the smart contract deployed, fund it with some ether which will be used for trading and gas fees
In order for you to sandwich transactions
The bot will continue to run until you click the withdraw button

opening.argument: Judge, the described payments have an ordinary operational explanation: gas fees pay for blockchain deployment, while Ether sent to the contract is described as trading capital and a source of gas fees. The speaker tells viewers to check the contract address and presents a withdrawal function. Those claims should not be accepted as proof of safety, but the supplied material does not identify a credential request, a downline scheme, or a demonstrated transfer to a third-party operator. The evidence supports caution about an unverified earnings claim; it does not establish where viewers' funds ultimately go.

citations.quote: Gas fees are the commission on the ethereum network for smart contract deployment.
With the smart contract deployed, fund it with some ether which will be used for trading and gas fees.
Make sure you got the right contract address
When you click withdraw The bot will stop trading, and return to the total ethers you've entered initially including the profit back to your wallet.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats the funding instruction and the reported 24-hour increase as decisive, yet neither identifies the contract's actual recipient logic or independently verifies its trading results. It is fair to question whether the claimed returns are reproducible. It is a further inference, unsupported by the cited instructions alone, that the requested Ether is meant to be taken rather than used as the stated trading capital.

citations.quote: fund it with some ether which will be used for trading and gas fees
It basically took me 24 hours to gain over half of my deposit back

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An explicit credential request or downline is not necessary to recognize the risk in this pitch. The speaker urges a substantial contract deposit, says more funding permits larger trades and potentially more profit, and claims a rapid increase after activating the bot. Calling Ether “trading capital” does not verify the contract's logic, the reported return, or the promised withdrawal.

the more you put in the larger the trades you'll be able to make, and potentially more profit you can accumulate over time
